entries.title: Apply MIP Labels to Multiple Files in Resource Inventory
body: You can now manually apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MIP) labels to multiple files in the on-premises file shares on the Resource Inventory page. This allows you to classify and protect files containing sensitive data.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details.

entries.title: Azure Application Discovery
body: DSPM investigates the service principal metadata and discovers Azure applications and categorizes them as:
- Internal applications
- Third-party applications
- Microsoft applications
- System-assigned managed identity
- User-assigned managed identity
- AI agent identity
This information is displayed in the Resource Inventory graph, giving you visibility into the Azure applications that have access to resources and data in your environment.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Graph for Azure Data Stores.

entries.title: Compliance Dashboard Enhancements
body: The Compliance dashboard includes the following enhancements:
- A new tab, Findings, is available listing the open issues for specific resources and for the selected compliance framework.
- See image.

- The Saved View option is available for all the tabs. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized page view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.
- See image.

- The Data Stores column on the Policies tab is clickable. Clicking the number of data stores redirects you to the Findings tab to view the resources that are noncompliant, along with the policy ID pre-selected.
- See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Compliance Details.

entries.title: GCP Single Project Onboarding
body: DSPM now supports the onboarding of Google Cloud Platform (GCP) single projects to monitor and scan the data stores within them. This option can be used when there are restrictions for onboarding projects at the organization level.
See image.
To learn more, see Onboarding a GCP Project.

entries.title: ZAgent Skills for Data Protection
body: ZAgent is powered by agentic AI to enhance the capabilities of the AI virtual assistant that is dedicated to troubleshooting multistep tasks and answering complex questions. You can select the predefined Data Protection as an agent to jumpstart your AI workflow to access Zscaler's knowledge base or analyze data to understand the data protection of your organization's multi-cloud platforms.
See image.
To learn more, see About ZAgent and Understanding ZAgent with Use Cases.

entries.title: Azure Single Subscription Onboarding
body: DSPM now supports the onboarding of Azure single subscriptions to monitor and scan the data stores within them. This option can be used when there are restrictions for onboarding subscriptions at the tenant or management group level.
See image.
To learn more, see Onboarding an Azure Subscription.

entries.title: Manual File Actions in Data Inventory
body: You can now manually apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MIP) labels to single or multiple on-premises file shares created on file servers and Azure file shares. This allows you to review and remediate files containing sensitive data. Users with the Actions Apply Label permission can apply the labels.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Inventory.

entries.title: SaaS Overview Dashboard
body: The SaaS Overview dashboard is now moved under DSPM. The SaaS Overview dashboard visually displays the detected incidents, showing their distribution and identifying affected applications and users. You can view the total number of SaaS incidents, list of user accounts with the most number of SaaS incidents, and SaaS applications containing sensitive data that are publicly exposed to the internet. This information allows you to identify the overall security risk and prioritize mitigation based on the incident type and affected entities.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the SaaS Overview Dashboard.

entries.title: Saved Views in Alerts and Data Duplications
body: The Saved Views option is available for Alerts and Data Duplications. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized page view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Alerts and About Data Duplications.

entries.title: Snowflake Database Graph Enhancement
body: The graph for Snowflake database includes a public internet node that provides visibility of databases that are publicly exposed to the internet.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Graph for Databases.

entries.title: Data Duplication Report for SaaS
body: The Data Duplications Report and the Data Duplications tab display files detected in SaaS services for subscriptions that include both DSPM and out-of-the-box (OOB) CASB. You can review identical files across cloud services, on-premises file shares, and SaaS services such as M365, JIRA, Google Drive, and Salesforce.
See image.
To learn more, see About Data Duplications.

entries.title: Identity Inventory Enhancements
body: The Identity Inventory is now more intuitive with clearer, human-readable entity information, new ways to view and filter identities by category, source, and cloud service providers. These improvements are also available in the Access tab on the Resource Inventory page.
The Identity Inventory includes the following new columns:
- Entity Source: The repository (e.g., AWS Cloud Resource, EntraID) where the identity data is stored.
- Entity Category: The entity category (e.g., External users, Services).
- Target Environment: The cloud service providers (e.g., GCP) that the identity can access.
See image.
To learn more, see About Identity Inventory and Viewing the Access Levels.

entries.title: Saved Views in the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory
body: Saved Views functionality is available for the Data Inventory and Resource Inventory. You can apply filters, show or hide columns in the table, and save this page setting. This allows you to return to the same customized view without having to reapply the settings each time you visit the page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Resource Inventory and Viewing the Data Inventory.

entries.title: Support for Selecting DLP Engines to Scan Data
body: Zscaler DLP engines are configured centrally and used for DLP classification engines across channels such as web, email, DSPM, endpoints, and SaaS Security. You can now select specific DLP engines for DSPM and reduce the extra noise from other DLP engines applied to other channels.
All existing DLP engines are assigned to DSPM by default. You can enable or disable the DSPM channel in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding DLP Engines and Dictionaries and Editing Predefined DLP Engines.

entries.title: Unified Dashboard Enhancements
body: Links are added to the Top Sensitive Data At Rest section in the Unified dashboard. This allows you to investigate the relevant files and database tables. For data stored in public cloud and on-premises environments, these links navigate to the Data Inventory.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Security Dashboard.

entries.title: Data Inventory Enhancements
body: Data Inventory includes the following enhancements:
# SaaS Data in the Data Inventory

Zscaler has now unified data-at-rest findings under DSPM, bringing together cloud, on-premises, and SaaS data into the same reports and workflows. Customers subscribed to Out-of-Band CASB can view the SaaS data findings within the Data Inventory report. This allows you to explore sensitive data findings in files stored on clouds, on-premises, and SaaS applications in a single report.
See image.
# Entitlement Findings in On-Premises SMB File Shares

DSPM provides support to scan the on-premises SMB file shares and detect identities (users, groups, and computer accounts) that have access to sensitive data. This allows you to review and restrict specific identities from accessing sensitive data.
See image.
To enable this scan, you must register a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server and associate it with your on-premises file servers.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Data Inventory, Adding an LDAP Server, and Adding an On-Premises File Server.

entries.title: Data Scan Enhancements
body: Data scanning includes the following enhancements:
# RDBMS Data Sample Scanning

When performing a data sampling scan on Relational Database Management Systems (RDBMS), random rows are selected from each table. This provides a more accurate representation of data, reduces scan times and less impact on large databases.
To learn more, see About Scan Settings.
# Predefined Data Classification Engines

DSPM provides 70 predefined data classification engines for common sensitive data types, such as credit cards, Social Security numbers (SSNs), national IDs, and driver's licenses. These engines are built with high accuracy and help reduce false positives. You can select the engines while configuring the scan scope.
To learn more, see Understanding Data Classification and About Data Sensitivity Settings.

entries.title: DSPM Upgraded to Experience Center

To learn more, see About On-Premises Data Centers, Managing an On-Premises Data Center, Adding Unmanaged Databases, and Editing or Deleting Unmanaged Databases.

entries.title: Data Scan Enhancements
body: Data scanning includes the following enhancements:
# Support for On-Premises NetApp File Shares
DSPM supports the discovery and classification of sensitive data in on-premises NetApp file shares using NFS and SMB protocols.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding an On-Premises File Server.
# Column-Level Scanning for Databases
DSPM provides visibility into all columns that contain sensitive data, precisely matching the data types with the specific columns in the database table.
You can view the results of column-level scanning on:
- Data Tab: View column-level sensitive data classifications and the associated DLP dictionaries.
- See image.
- Column-Specific Evidence Tab: View the evidence details based on the column-level scanning, organized by column and DLP dictionary for detailed investigation.
- See image.
# OCR Scan for Embedded Images
DSPM supports Optical Character Recognition (OCR) scanning to scan and identify sensitive data in images embedded in files (PDF, Word, PPT, etc.).
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details and Viewing the Data Inventory.

entries.title: Discovery Status and Error Messages for On-Premises File Servers

See image.
To learn more, see About Service Registration.

entries.title: Microsoft 365 Tenant Onboarding

entries.title: MIP Labeling Enhancements
body: The following enhancements are included:
# MIP Labeling for On-Premises File Shares

DSPM extends Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labeling for on-premises SMB and NFS file shares. Use action rules to automatically apply MIP sensitivity labels to sensitive data (e.g., PII, PHI, PCI).
See image.
To learn more, see About Action Rules and Adding Action Rules.
# File Activity Tab

You can view the activities related to applying MIP labeling on the File Activity tab. You can see what action was performed (e.g., Apply Label), the entity that performed the action (e.g., Zscaler), and the timestamp.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Sensitive Data Details and Viewing the Data Inventory.

entries.title: Action Rules
body: Action rules allow you to define the criteria for identifying specific data types and to automatically apply Microsoft Information Protection sensitivity labels to files. This feature currently supports Azure File Shares
See image.
To learn more, see About Action Rules.

entries.title: Additional Threat Categories

- AI Safety

entries.title: AI Security
body: DSPM AI security includes the following enhancements:
# Scanning AI Models

DSPM scans AI models to identify vulnerabilities such as malicious code injection, backdoors, embedded secrets, data leakage, etc. The scan results are displayed on the AI Model Security Scan Findings page.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Scan Results for AI Models, About Scanning AI Models, Deploying the AI Model Scanner, and Managing AI Model Scan Integrations.
# Scanning AWS ECR Images for Vulnerabilities
DSPM provides support to scan AWS ECR images, and provides visibility into model usage, licensing, versions, and security vulnerabilities across containerized machine learning workloads.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for AWS ECR Images.
# Support for Azure AI Agents
DSPM provides visibility into deployed Azure AI Agents and the sensitive data they have access to.
See image.
To learn more, see Managing Services.
# Visibility into Google Cloud Vertex AI
DSPM supports the discovery of GCP Vertex AI and its access to sensitive data, as well as determining entitlement and posture.
To learn more, see Onboarding a GCP Organization.

entries.title: Data Scanning Enhancements
body: The following enhancements are made to data scanning:
# On-Demand Scanning

You can now use the On-Demand scan option to run the scans manually. This is supported for all resource types including virtual machines, databases, NoSQL databases and unmanaged databases. Use this option only when ad hoc scans are required.
See image.
# Data Scanning Inclusions and Exclusions
In addition to multiple existing scan settings options to include and exclude data stores in data scanning, the following options are available:
- Specific virtual machines and databases can be included in the scan settings.
- See image.
- Cloud resource tags can be used as the exclusion factor, allowing to exclude resources with certain tags from scanning.
- See image.
# Scan Setting UI Enhancements
You can select specific resources while configuring the scan settings.
See image.
# Scan Start Time Configuration for Unmanaged Databases
You can configure a specific time window for scanning unmanaged databases so that the scans run when databases are least used, reducing any performance impact during active periods.
See image.
# Stop In-Progress Scans
Scheduled or on-demand scans that are currently in progress can be stopped for the following resources:
- Virtual machines
- Managed and unmanaged databases
- NoSQL data stores
See image.
To learn more, see Starting or Stopping a Scan, and About Scan Settings.

entries.title: Database Enhancements
body: The following are the database enhancements:
# Snowflake Database Support
Zscaler DSPM now supports Snowflake and scans databases within the onboarded Snowflake accounts for sensitive data and provides security assessments.
See image.
To learn more, see About Snowflake, Adding Snowflake Database Account, and Configuring Scan Settings for Snowflake Databases.
# HashiCorp Vault for Secret Storage
HashiCorp's self-hosted secret store HashiCorp Vault is now supported for hosting keys used for database scanning.

Tokens and secrets used for database access are typically stored in CSP-based secret stores, such as Amazon secret manager or Azure Key Vault. DSPM uses these storages to gain secure access to scan unmanaged databases running in CSPs or on-premises.
See image.
To learn more, see Adding Unmanaged Databases.

The Timeline tab displays Azure and GCP event details such as configuration and management changes for a specific time period, who made the change, what was the change, when it was made, etc.

entries.title: Scan Support for Additional Databases
body: DSPM provides support for scanning the following databases in AWS and Azure cloud environments:
- Unmanaged MySQL Database

entries.title: Data Scan Enhancements
body: The data scan includes the following enhancements:
# Support for Scanning GCP Compute Engines

DSPM scans and classifies the data in disks associated with GCP compute engines, checks for misconfigurations and posture issues, performs vulnerability analysis, checks for access and entitlements issues, and runs dedicated predefined policies. GCP compute engines can now be explored and investigated on the dashboard, and the Data Inventory and Alerts pages. To learn more, see Configuring Scan Settings for GCP Virtual Machine.
# On-Premises Database Scanning for MSSQL

DSPM provides support for on-premises database scanning. DSPM can perform remote agentless scanning of the MSSQL database servers stored in private and public data centers. This enables the scanning of sensitive data in unmanaged databases. Databases can be assigned to data center objects for ease of reporting. Scan settings can be configured to define the scan scope and frequency.

# Predicates for Unmanaged PostgreSQL

To learn more, see Creating an Investigation and Creating Custom Policies.
# Predicates for GCP Compute VM
You can use the following relationship predicates to query the GCP Compute VM:
- Can be accessed by
- Has Entitlement
- Has Access to
To learn more, see Creating an Investigation.
# Predicate for AI Service

The Exposed to AI service predicate allows you to check whether any storage account containing sensitive data is exposed to an AI service. The exposure could be through a permission or an access configuration in the AI service or a combination of both.
To learn more, see Viewing Graph for AI Services.

entries.title: AI Service Details in Data Inventory

Sensitive data exposed to AI services is at risk of unwanted public exposure to AI service users and applications. DSPM analyzes the permissions and configurations that lead to exposing data stores containing sensitive data to the AI service. entries.title: Investigation and Policy Query Enhancements
body: Additional operators are available when creating an investigation or policy query:
# Fixed and Relative Time Operators
The following operators are available for the Date predicate:
- Fixed time operators (related to a specific date)
- = : On (a specific date)
- |...| : Between (specific dates)
- ⇠| : Before a specific date
- ⇢| : After a specific date
- Relative time operators
- < : Less than (x days)
- > : More than (x days)
# Included In Operator
For the Resource Property predicate, you can use the Included In (⊆ ) operator for Boolean values. This allows you to create queries with combinations of Null (∅), Doesn't Exist, and Boolean values.
To learn more, see Creating a New Investigation and Creating Custom Policies.
# Investigate Secondary Resources Attached to Primary Resource

When creating a custom policy or investigation, you can query secondary and tertiary cloud service provider (CSP) resources attached to the primary resource. This allows DSPM to access and detect risks in the secondary or tertiary resources (e.g., virtual machines and network security groups, or EC2 instance and network interface). You can use the Associated With predicate and leverage the resource relationships.
See image.
To learn more, see Creating a New Investigation and Creating Custom Policies.

entries.title: Azure SQL Server Support
